transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes, there are two key things to clean. The 'funny smell' is probably lint or fluff scorching on the heating element because airflow is restricted. Please unplug the machine for safety, then remove and wash the main lint filter (usually behind a small flap at the bottom front). Most Hotpoint washer-dryers also have a condenser unit inside that same compartment which needs rinsing under the tap to remove fine fluff. Also ensure you are not drying more than half the washing load capacity; if you put in 8kg of wet clothes, it will likely remain damp because the dryer can only handle about 5kg.
Ok, I'll try that. It smells like burning dust or scorched fabric, and the top of the machine gets very hot during drying. I've kept using it though. I usually dry a full 8-9kg wash load in one go.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Please stop using the machine immediately. This is a fire hazard. Even if you clean the filter now, the machine needs a qualified engineer to check for damage to the heater, thermal cut-out, and internal wiring before it can be used safely again.
